en.greeting: Hi! At B1 you used who, which, that and where to say which person or thing you mean. Today we go further: extra information with commas, whose, whom, which for a whole idea, and shorter clauses. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Two kinds of relative clause
steps.text: Quick recap first, then something new.
steps.body: At B1, *the man **who lives next door*** tells us **which** man: no commas. New: a **non-defining** clause adds **extra information** about someone we already know, between **commas**, like brackets: *My father, **who lives in Bandung**, is a doctor.* You have one father, so it's a bonus fact. Without commas, *My father who lives in Bandung…* sounds as if you have **several fathers**! In speech, the commas are short pauses.

pairs.en: My father, who lives in Bandung, is a doctor.
pairs.id: Ayah saya, yang tinggal di Bandung, adalah dokter. (info tambahan → koma)

pairs.en: the man who lives next door
pairs.id: pria yang tinggal di sebelah (yang mana? → tanpa koma)

pairs.en: Bandung, where I grew up,
pairs.id: Bandung, tempat saya dibesarkan, (nama → sudah jelas)

steps.title: With commas: two rules
steps.text: Read these. Look at the word right after the first comma.
steps.body: Between commas: **who** for people, **which** for things, **where** for places, but **never that**. And **never leave the word out**, even when *I* or *we* comes next (*Dimas, **who** I worked with…*).

examples.en: Pak Hasan, who has worked here for twenty years, is retiring next month.
examples.id: Pak Hasan, yang sudah bekerja di sini selama dua puluh tahun, akan pensiun bulan depan.

examples.en: Our office, which is on the 12th floor, has a great view.
examples.id: Kantor kami, yang ada di lantai 12, pemandangannya bagus. (bukan ', that')

examples.en: Dimas, who I worked with in Surabaya, now lives in Singapore.
examples.id: Dimas, yang dulu bekerja bersama saya di Surabaya, sekarang tinggal di Singapura. (who tidak boleh hilang)

examples.en: My sister who lives in Medan is a nurse.
examples.id: Saudara perempuan saya yang tinggal di Medan adalah perawat. (tanpa koma: saudara perempuan saya lebih dari satu)

examples.en: My sister, who lives in Medan, is a nurse.
examples.id: Saudara perempuan saya, yang tinggal di Medan, adalah perawat. (pakai koma: cuma satu)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Think: does the clause say which one, or is it a bonus fact?

question.prompt: Sari is talking about her mother. Which sentence is correct?
options: My mother, that teaches English, lives in Solo.
My mother, who teaches English, lives in Solo.
My mother who teaches English lives in Solo.
question.explanation: Sari has only one mother, so *who teaches English* is extra information and goes between **commas**. **that** is never used between commas, and without commas it sounds as if she has several mothers.

steps.title: whose and whom
steps.text: Two more words for your relative clauses.
steps.body: **whose** = Indonesian **yang …-nya** (belonging): *pria yang mobil**nya** dicuri* → *the man **whose** car was stolen* (not *'who his car'*). Don't mix it up with **who's** = who is. **whom** is a formal **who** for the person who receives the action, mostly after *to, with, for*: *the client **to whom** I sent the invoice*. In speech just say *the client I sent the invoice to*. Never *'to who'*.

pairs.en: the man whose car was stolen
pairs.id: pria yang mobilnya dicuri

pairs.en: a startup whose app is used by millions
pairs.id: startup yang aplikasinya dipakai jutaan orang

pairs.en: the client to whom I sent the invoice
pairs.id: klien yang saya kirimi tagihan (formal)

pairs.en: the client I sent the invoice to
pairs.id: klien yang saya kirimi tagihan (sehari-hari)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Whose laptop is it?

question.prompt: I'm looking for the student ___ laptop was left in the meeting room.
options: who
who's
whose
question.explanation: The laptop belongs to the student (*mahasiswa yang laptopnya tertinggal*), so use **whose**. **who's** means *who is*, and **who** can't show belonging.

steps.title: which for a whole idea
steps.text: Sometimes which doesn't point to one thing, but to everything before it.
steps.body: *He didn't call, **which** was strange.* What was strange? **The fact that he didn't call**: the whole idea. Indonesian says *…, dan itu aneh*. In English use a **comma + which**. Not *what*, not *that*, and not *', it was strange'* (that's two sentences joined only by a comma).

pairs.en: He didn't call, which was strange.
pairs.id: Dia tidak menelepon, dan itu aneh.

pairs.en: Rina passed the exam, which made her parents very proud.
pairs.id: Rina lulus ujian, dan itu membuat orang tuanya sangat bangga.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: What does the missing word refer to?

question.prompt: The lift was broken, ___ meant we had to walk up to the 12th floor.
options: which
what
that
question.explanation: **which** refers to the whole idea (*the lift was broken*). **what** isn't used like this, and **that** can't follow a comma here. (*lift* is British; Americans say *elevator*.)

steps.title: Shorter clauses
steps.text: Good writers and speakers often make relative clauses shorter.
steps.body: When **who/which** is followed by **is/are/was/were**, drop **both words**: *the man **who is standing** there* → *the man **standing** there*; *the report **which was written** by Rina* → *the report **written** by Rina* (**V3**, the passive form: Rina wrote it). Drop both, not just one: *'The man is standing there is my boss'* ✗, *'the report which written'* ✗.

pairs.en: the man standing there
pairs.id: pria yang berdiri di sana (= who is standing)

pairs.en: the report written by Rina
pairs.id: laporan yang ditulis oleh Rina (= which was written)

pairs.en: people waiting for the KRL
pairs.id: orang-orang yang sedang menunggu KRL (= who are waiting)

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Make it short and natural: no who, no is.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kamu kenal pria yang sedang menunggu di lobi?
question.solution: Do you know the man waiting in the lobby?
question.explanation: *the man waiting in the lobby* = *the man **who is waiting** in the lobby*. Drop **who is** and keep **waiting**.

steps.title: Spot the correct one
steps.text: One sentence drops both words. Which one?

options: The contract which signed yesterday is on your desk.
The contract was signed yesterday is on your desk.
The contract signed yesterday is on your desk.
question.explanation: The full version is *the contract **which was signed** yesterday*. To make it shorter, drop **which was** and keep *signed* (V3). The other two drop only one word, which leaves a broken sentence.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Advanced relative clauses
artifact.intro: Commas for extra information, whose, whom, which for a whole idea, and shorter clauses.
rows: the man who lives next door
My father, who lives in Bandung, is a doctor.
Our office, which is on the 12th floor, has a great view.
the man whose car was stolen
the client to whom I sent the invoice
He didn't call, which was strange.
tips: Between commas: never that, and never leave who or which out.
Shorter clause: drop who/which AND is/are/was/were, not just one of them.

examples.en: My father, who lives in Bandung, is a doctor.
examples.id: Ayah saya, yang tinggal di Bandung, adalah dokter.

examples.en: He didn't call, which was strange.
examples.id: Dia tidak menelepon, dan itu aneh.

examples.en: The report written by Rina was excellent.
examples.id: Laporan yang ditulis oleh Rina bagus sekali.

id.greeting: Hai! Di B1 kamu sudah memakai who, which, that dan where untuk menjelaskan orang atau benda yang mana yang kamu maksud. Hari ini kita lanjut: informasi tambahan dengan koma, whose, whom, which untuk seluruh ide, dan klausa yang diringkas. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Dua jenis relative clause
steps.text: Kita ulang sebentar, lalu lanjut ke hal baru.
steps.body: Di B1, *the man **who lives next door*** menjelaskan pria **yang mana**: tanpa koma. Baru: **non-defining** clause menambahkan **informasi tambahan** tentang orang yang sudah jelas, di antara **koma**, seperti tanda kurung: *My father, **who lives in Bandung**, is a doctor.* Ayahmu cuma satu, jadi itu info bonus. Tanpa koma, *My father who lives in Bandung…* terdengar seolah ayahmu **lebih dari satu**! Saat bicara, koma itu jadi jeda singkat.

pairs.en: My father, who lives in Bandung, is a doctor.
pairs.id: Ayah saya, yang tinggal di Bandung, adalah dokter. (info tambahan → koma)

pairs.en: the man who lives next door
pairs.id: pria yang tinggal di sebelah (yang mana? → tanpa koma)

pairs.en: Bandung, where I grew up,
pairs.id: Bandung, tempat saya dibesarkan, (nama → sudah jelas)

steps.title: Dengan koma: dua aturan
steps.text: Baca contoh-contoh ini. Perhatikan kata tepat setelah koma pertama.
steps.body: Di antara koma: **who** untuk orang, **which** untuk benda, **where** untuk tempat, tapi **tidak pernah that**. Dan katanya **tidak boleh dihilangkan**, walaupun setelahnya ada *I* atau *we* (*Dimas, **who** I worked with…*).

examples.en: Pak Hasan, who has worked here for twenty years, is retiring next month.
examples.id: Pak Hasan, yang sudah bekerja di sini selama dua puluh tahun, akan pensiun bulan depan.

examples.en: Our office, which is on the 12th floor, has a great view.
examples.id: Kantor kami, yang ada di lantai 12, pemandangannya bagus. (bukan ', that')

examples.en: Dimas, who I worked with in Surabaya, now lives in Singapore.
examples.id: Dimas, yang dulu bekerja bersama saya di Surabaya, sekarang tinggal di Singapura. (who tidak boleh hilang)

examples.en: My sister who lives in Medan is a nurse.
examples.id: Saudara perempuan saya yang tinggal di Medan adalah perawat. (tanpa koma: saudara perempuan saya lebih dari satu)

examples.en: My sister, who lives in Medan, is a nurse.
examples.id: Saudara perempuan saya, yang tinggal di Medan, adalah perawat. (pakai koma: cuma satu)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pikirkan: apakah klausanya menjelaskan yang mana, atau hanya info bonus?

question.prompt: Sari sedang bercerita tentang ibunya. Kalimat mana yang benar?
options: My mother, that teaches English, lives in Solo.
My mother, who teaches English, lives in Solo.
My mother who teaches English lives in Solo.
question.explanation: Ibu Sari cuma satu, jadi *who teaches English* adalah info tambahan dan diletakkan di antara **koma**. **that** tidak pernah dipakai di antara koma, dan tanpa koma kalimatnya terdengar seolah ibunya lebih dari satu.

steps.title: whose dan whom
steps.text: Dua kata lagi untuk relative clause-mu.
steps.body: **whose** = **yang …-nya** (kepemilikan): *pria yang mobil**nya** dicuri* → *the man **whose** car was stolen* (bukan *'who his car'*). Jangan tertukar dengan **who's** = who is. **whom** adalah **who** versi formal untuk orang yang dikenai tindakan, biasanya setelah *to, with, for*: *the client **to whom** I sent the invoice*. Saat bicara cukup *the client I sent the invoice to*. Jangan pernah *'to who'*.

pairs.en: the man whose car was stolen
pairs.id: pria yang mobilnya dicuri

pairs.en: a startup whose app is used by millions
pairs.id: startup yang aplikasinya dipakai jutaan orang

pairs.en: the client to whom I sent the invoice
pairs.id: klien yang saya kirimi tagihan (formal)

pairs.en: the client I sent the invoice to
pairs.id: klien yang saya kirimi tagihan (sehari-hari)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Laptop siapa itu?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: I'm looking for the student ___ laptop was left in the meeting room.
options: who
who's
whose
question.explanation: Laptop itu milik mahasiswa tersebut (*mahasiswa yang laptopnya tertinggal*), jadi pakai **whose**. **who's** artinya *who is*, dan **who** tidak bisa menunjukkan kepemilikan.

steps.title: which untuk seluruh ide
steps.text: Kadang which tidak menunjuk satu benda, tapi semua yang ada sebelumnya.
steps.body: *He didn't call, **which** was strange.* Apa yang aneh? **Kenyataan bahwa dia tidak menelepon**: seluruh idenya. Bahasa Indonesia bilang *…, dan itu aneh*. Dalam bahasa Inggris pakai **koma + which**. Bukan *what*, bukan *that*, dan bukan *', it was strange'* (itu dua kalimat yang disambung hanya dengan koma).

pairs.en: He didn't call, which was strange.
pairs.id: Dia tidak menelepon, dan itu aneh.

pairs.en: Rina passed the exam, which made her parents very proud.
pairs.id: Rina lulus ujian, dan itu membuat orang tuanya sangat bangga.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kata yang hilang itu merujuk ke apa?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: The lift was broken, ___ meant we had to walk up to the 12th floor.
options: which
what
that
question.explanation: **which** merujuk seluruh ide (*lift-nya rusak*). **what** tidak dipakai seperti ini, dan **that** tidak bisa dipakai setelah koma di sini. (*lift* adalah bahasa Inggris Britania; orang Amerika bilang *elevator*.)

steps.title: Klausa yang diringkas
steps.text: Penulis dan pembicara yang baik sering meringkas relative clause.
steps.body: Kalau setelah **who/which** ada **is/are/was/were**, buang **kedua kata itu**: *the man **who is standing** there* → *the man **standing** there*; *the report **which was written** by Rina* → *the report **written** by Rina* (**V3**, bentuk pasif: Rina yang menulis). Buang dua-duanya, jangan cuma satu: *'The man is standing there is my boss'* ✗, *'the report which written'* ✗.

pairs.en: the man standing there
pairs.id: pria yang berdiri di sana (= who is standing)

pairs.en: the report written by Rina
pairs.id: laporan yang ditulis oleh Rina (= which was written)

pairs.en: people waiting for the KRL
pairs.id: orang-orang yang sedang menunggu KRL (= who are waiting)

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Buat ringkas dan natural: tanpa who, tanpa is.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kamu kenal pria yang sedang menunggu di lobi?
question.solution: Do you know the man waiting in the lobby?
question.explanation: *the man waiting in the lobby* = *the man **who is waiting** in the lobby*. Buang **who is** dan pertahankan **waiting**.

steps.title: Mana yang benar?
steps.text: Satu kalimat membuang kedua kata. Yang mana?

options: The contract which signed yesterday is on your desk.
The contract was signed yesterday is on your desk.
The contract signed yesterday is on your desk.
question.explanation: Versi lengkapnya *the contract **which was signed** yesterday*. Untuk meringkasnya, buang **which was** dan pertahankan *signed* (V3). Dua kalimat lainnya hanya membuang satu kata, jadi kalimatnya rusak.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman.
